Hurricane Milton Discussion Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL142024
400 AM CDT Tue Oct 08 2024

Air Force Hurricane Hunters and NOAA aircraft have been investigating
Milton overnight, and reports indicate that the hurricane has continued
to slowly strengthen. The eye has remained warm and well-defined on
satellite imagery, surrounded by a small ring of very cold cloud tops.
Subjective Dvorak intensity estimates from TAFB and SAB at 0600 UTC
were T7.0/140 kt. The latest Air Force flight measured a peak SFMR
wind of 142 kt and a minimum central pressure of 905 mb. Based on
this data, the initial intensity is set at 140 kt for this advisory.

Milton has finally turned eastward, and the latest motion estimate is
090/8 kt. A mid-level subtropical ridge to the north of the hurricane
should continue to steer Milton toward the east-northeast and
northeast through Wednesday, with the storm reaching the west coast
of Florida by late Wednesday or Wednesday night. The track guidance
remains in good agreement, and the official forecast has not changed
much from the previous advisory.

Some fluctuations in intensity are likely today, but Milton is
forecast to remain a powerful hurricane until landfall. Increasing
southwesterly shear and drier mid-level air should lead to weakening
on Wednesday, but Milton is still expected to be a major hurricane
when it reaches the Florida coast. After landfall, rapid weakening
is anticipated as the cyclone moves across the Florida peninsula and
emerges over the Atlantic Ocean late Thursday.


KEY MESSAGES:

1. Milton remains an extremely dangerous category 5 hurricane.

2. A life-threatening storm surge is expected along much of the
   west coast of the Florida Peninsula on Wednesday and Wednesday
   night.

3. Damaging hurricane-force winds are likely on the west coast of
   Florida by late Wednesday.
